Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday — PolyHealth is close to finalizing the security review but we hit two items that need clarification before legal signs the DPA addendum. Can you confirm the following?:

1) Current subprocessor list + airports of processing: we need a CSV list that shows which subprocessors may process EU personal data, which of those are used for caching/edge, and any onshore fallback you maintain.

2) SCCs vs UK IDTA: for UK-resident patient data where both SCCs and the UK Addendum could apply, what is Redwood's precedence / execution path? Legal wants to know whether we should expect a separate UK IDTA or if your SCC execution includes the addendum as standard.

3) Contingency if a subprocessor is terminated mid-contract: PolyHealth requires an explicit rollback/failover walk-through for any subprocessor termination that affects routing (e.g., if an edge cache provider is decommissioned).

Can you provide a single evidence packet or matrix and a suggested timeline for these asks? We have a compliance gate on Friday, 27 Jun.

Thanks,
Alice
Alice Monroe
Head of Privacy & Compliance
PolyHealth

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Kimberly from Legal and Laura from Product (infra) to make sure we fully cover the technical and contractual angles.

Quick summary answer while we pull attachments:
- We can provide a subprocessor inventory CSV that flags EU vs non-EU processing and identifies edge cache roles.
- Redwood executes standard EU SCCs for transfers; for UK-resident data we offer the UK IDTA (UK Addendum) as an explicit execution path — we do not rely on SCCs alone to satisfy UK contractual asks. Where customers require, we execute the UK Addendum alongside SCCs.
- For subprocessor termination that impacts routing, we maintain an onshore fallback policy (onshore cache or regional failover) and documented rollback steps; we will provide the step-by-step procedure and the retention/ingress implications.

We aim to get an evidence matrix (SCCs-UKAddendum-evidence-matrix.xlsx) + the subprocessor CSV to you by end of day Thursday 26 Jun. If you need it sooner for the Friday gate, we can accelerate.

Kimberly and Laura — can you confirm the contingency flows and whether the matrix needs any procurement-specific fields (DocuSign sign dates, vendor SLA links)?

Regards,

On Thu, Jun 26, 2025 at 08:22 AM Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Alice — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Kimberly from Legal and Laura from Product (infra) to make sure we fully cover the technical and contractual angles.

Hi all — adding legal detail and confirming evidence we will produce.

1) Subprocessor inventory: attached CSV will include columns: vendor_name, role, processing_location_countries, eu_processing_flag (Y/N), edge_cache_flag (Y/N), sla_link, onboarding_contract_date. We will mark any processors that have access to token-level logs.

2) SCCs vs UK IDTA: Redwood has two deployment patterns for customers with UK data residency concerns:
   - Default: execute EU SCCs for transfers and provide a separate UK Addendum upon request (standard contract path for UK residents).
   - Opt-in: for customers that prefer, we can execute the UK Addendum together with SCCs at signature (no additional engineering work required beyond ops checklist).

We will not claim that an EU SCC alone satisfies UK Addendum contractual language — we provide the Addendum as the formal instrument when required. Where PolyHealth wants the Addendum in place now, we will route a DPA addendum for signature.

3) Subprocessor termination & contingency: documented failover steps are included in the attached evidence matrix. Key points:
   - If an edge cache subprocessor is terminated, traffic is automatically routed to regional onshore caches where available (configurable per-customer).
   - We maintain a two-week contiguous rollback window for model KV cache consistency; beyond that, warm-up latency is expected and documented.
   - Legal will provide a termination notification template and a vendor replacement cadence (30/60/90) for procurement.

Deliverables
- SCCs-UKAddendum-evidence-matrix.xlsx (attached) — includes mapping to artifacts (SOC 2 report page refs, keystore attestations, KMS locations).
- redwood-subprocessor-inventory.csv (attached)
- mutual-action-plan-PH-8342.md (attached) — includes signing timeline and responsibilities.

Alice — if you want the matrix annotated against your internal DPIA fields, tell us which columns to map and we will add them.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Legal Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference

Attachments: SCCs-UKAddendum-evidence-matrix.xlsx (xlsx stub); redwood-subprocessor-inventory.csv (csv stub); mutual-action-plan-PH-8342.md (md stub)
